data.narrative: The student chose cache-aside, wired a redis-py client with a 0.2s ping, and fell back to an in-process TTL map because localhost:6379 is down. They proved miss/set/hit in logs, PATCH invalidation (stale Location when skipped, new Location when restored), and the abuse-spike 429 loop. They did not claim a live Redis HIT.

dimension_scores.observation: Picked cache-aside so Redis-down is a miss plus store read, not a failed write-through.
dimension_scores.evidence: DECIDE A; REDIS_DOWN True and redirects still 307 via cache_store_fallback redis_down=True.

dimension_scores.observation: Injected skipped PATCH invalidation, reproduced cache_hit to the old URL, then restored invalidate and re-ran the same script.
dimension_scores.evidence: BREAK_STALE True Location https://example.com/old; after FIX STALE_AVOIDED True Location https://example.org/new.

dimension_scores.observation: Cached only public redirect targets, not owner-scoped GET /links bodies; kept redirect rate limits for the abuse twist.
dimension_scores.evidence: ABUSE_REDIRECT_COUNTS 307x8 then 429x2; cache key is short_code only.

dimension_scores.observation: Named TTL 60s, key shape redir:{code}, Redis timeout 0.2s, and fallback instead of hanging on a dead Redis.
dimension_scores.evidence: cache.py socket_connect_timeout=0.2; first redirect logged TimeoutError then cache_miss backend=memory.

dimension_scores.observation: Separated Redis-down fallback from a fabricated cache hit and quoted miss/hit/invalidate log flags.
dimension_scores.evidence: module06_cache_verify.py prints LOG_CACHE_MISS/HIT/SET/INVALIDATE and LOG_REDIS_DOWN_FALLBACK True.

strengths: Stale-redirect regression is Location-based, not a comment.
Honest Redis-down drill: service already down, ping timed out, redirect still worked.
growth_areas: No single-flight lock on miss (thundering herd) because the SoT is in-process and fast; add a lock when Postgres is the miss path.
data.recommendation: When Redis is up, assert backend=redis on cache_hit and keep the memory fallback behind the same invalidate function so key shapes cannot drift.

public_evidence.student_action: Resolved GET /r/{code} through a TTL cache with Redis probe plus in-process fallback.
public_evidence.technical_detail: api/app/cache.py get/set/invalidate; redis-py from_url with 0.2s timeouts; TTL_S=60; key redir:{code}.
public_evidence.proof: module06_cache_verify.py: first redirect 307 miss+set, second 307 hit, REDIS_DOWN True, cache_redis_down_fallback logged.
public_evidence.ability: Adds caching without making the cache the source of truth.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the student can speed a hot path and still serve when the cache tier is down.

public_evidence.student_action: Updated long_url via PATCH /links/{code} and required cache drop so the next redirect uses the new Location.
public_evidence.technical_detail: update_link calls invalidate_redirect_target(code); delete paths do the same.
public_evidence.proof: Without invalidate, Location stayed https://example.com/old (BREAK_STALE True). With invalidate, Location became https://example.org/new (STALE_AVOIDED True).
public_evidence.ability: Treats cache invalidation as a write-path contract, not an optional cleanup.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Stale short links are a user-facing correctness bug, not just a performance miss.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Miss reads the store and set_redirect_target; hit returns without touching the store.
Skipping PATCH invalidate served the old URL; restoring it served the new URL.
Redis ping TimeoutError then memory backend; redirect still 307.

teaching_approaches.detail: Compared Location before/after PATCH with and without invalidate.
